body.x: When one cell in an electric vehicle (EV) or energy storage system (ESS) battery overheats, the question is how long the fire and heat take to reach the next cell, module and pack.
YeSUN Tech, a maker of functional adhesive materials, has developed a material aimed at that delay.

YeSUN Tech Co., Ltd., established in 2005 and led by CEO Choonsup Chun, is exhibiting at KES 2026 with Flame Barrier, a fire-resistant adhesive material for EV and ESS batteries which won a KES 2026 Innovation Award. The company is showing actual samples and application structures for battery cells, modules and packs, together with its functional adhesive components for OLED and LCD displays and high-reliability adhesive materials for automotive electronics.

Flame Barrier is engineered to delay fire propagation and heat transfer under high-temperature flame exposure. Depending on the battery structure and customer requirements, it can be combined with fire-resistant materials including mica, silicone, aramid and metal. YeSUN Tech tests the material by exposing it to a 1,300°C flame for 30 minutes. In June 2026, the company registered a Korean patent for a fire-resistant sheet for EV batteries with double fire-resistant adhesive layers and its manufacturing method.

The company applies the adhesive design, coating, lamination and precision converting expertise it built in displays and automotive electronics to battery safety. YeSUN Tech listed on the KOSDAQ market in 2019, has overseas production bases in Guangzhou and Suzhou in China, Hai Phong in Vietnam and Cikarang in Indonesia, and reached revenue of about KRW 66 billion (about USD 47 million) in 2021.

YeSUN Tech exports to more than six countries, including China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and the United States, and recorded about USD 11.22 million in exports in 2024, with China accounting for about 50%. It aims for about USD 13 million in exports in 2026, helped by growing sales of its foam pad products in the Chinese display market. The company plans to widen its export markets to regions including North America and develop Flame Barrier and automotive electronics materials as new export products. It names finding new customers and building local technical and sales networks as its main challenges, since new materials need evaluation and joint development tailored to each customer's product.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
